official.deadline_note: Applicants going through a Canadian institution with a doctoral award quota must meet that institution's internal deadline, which SSHRC warns is often significantly earlier; scholarship liaison officers may forward applications to SSHRC until 8:00 p.m. eastern on December 7, 2026.
official.status_note: SSHRC lists the October 2026 Competition with an application deadline of October 19, 2026 (8:00 p.m. eastern) and a value and duration of $40,000 per year for 3 years.
benefits: Value and duration of $40,000 per year for 3 years

Eligibility for associated supplements and joint initiatives, including the Indigenous Scholars Awards and Supplements Pilot Initiative ($5,000 one-year supplement for Indigenous CGRS-D holders), Mitacs Training, the DND MINDS Scholarship Initiative, the Aileen D. Ross Fellowship and the Queen's Fellowship
Additional award offers may be made for meritorious applications aligned with the eight published priority research areas
eligibility: Completed no more than 36 months of full-time-equivalent doctoral study by December 31 of the calendar year of application
Apply to only one Canada Research Training Awards Suite program per academic year
Maximum of three lifetime applications to the CGRS-D program
Must not already have received a doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC (including a Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship)

Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons apply through their institution if it holds a doctoral award quota, or directly to the agency otherwise; international applicants must be registered in a doctoral program at an eligible Canadian institution by the application deadline, and up to 15% of awards are available to international applicants

The doctoral program must be predominantly research-oriented and lead to a thesis, major research project, dissertation, scholarly publication, performance, recital or exhibit that is merit-reviewed by a panel of experts
requirements: Complete and verify the online CGRS-D application form and the SSHRC web-based curriculum vitae; every page must be marked 'Verify'
Two Letters of Appraisal of one page each, completed by referees through the online system before the deadline
Research proposal of maximum two pages (PDF, unprotected, maximum 500 Kb, 12 pt Times New Roman, single-spaced, minimum 3/4 inch margins)
Bibliography and works-cited file of maximum five pages
Up-to-date official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate studies
Research contributions, relevant experience and activities, maximum two pages combined
Certified English or French translation of any supporting document in another language
documents: Online application form generated in the SSHRC system
Research contributions and applicant statement (max 2 pages)
Two referee Letters of Appraisal (1 page each)
selection_criteria: Research potential, 50% - quality of the research proposal, feasibility, significance and expected contributions, judgement, ethical conduct, originality and communication
Relevant experience and achievements obtained within and beyond academia, 50% - academic record, training, scholarships, publications, teaching, mentoring, community outreach and other activities
coverage: Published value and duration of $40,000 per year for 3 years; the agencies publish no statement that tuition or other specific expenses are covered
application_method: Determine the correct channel from your registration status during the calendar year of application and whether the institution holds a doctoral award quota for your agency
Submit electronically through the SSHRC online system (Registration and login), with referees submitting their Letters of Appraisal through the same system
Applications submitted through the incorrect channel will not be considered
official.application_route: Apply online through the SSHRC system, either directly to SSHRC by 8:00 p.m. ET on October 19, 2026 or through a Canadian institution with a doctoral award quota by its own earlier deadline.
official.study_mode: Full-time study is the norm; tri-agency guidance notes award holders may be eligible to hold their awards part time
official.citizenship_residency: Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons may hold the award at any eligible Canadian degree-granting institution or, subject to conditions, outside Canada; international applicants must be registered at an eligible Canadian institution by the deadline
official.international_eligibility: Yes - up to 15% of CGRS-D awards are available to international applicants, who must be registered in a doctoral program at an eligible Canadian institution by the application deadline
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Apply to the federal granting agency best aligned with the research subject matter (CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC); applications submitted to the incorrect agency are deemed ineligible
official.research_requirement: A maximum two-page research proposal in plain language for a multidisciplinary committee, plus up to five pages of bibliography and works cited
official.description: The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship-Doctoral recognizes and supports the next generation of outstanding innovators, knowledge workers, creative thinkers and researchers by providing support for a high-quality research training experience. It is part of the Canada Research Training Awards Suite administered by CIHR, NSERC and SSHRC and supports research excellence across health, natural sciences and engineering, social sciences and humanities, including interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary research.
official.program_type: Federal research training award (Canada Research Training Awards Suite)
official.english_requirement: Applications may be submitted in English or French; supporting documents in a language other than English or French must be accompanied by a certified translation

not_confirmed: living_cost_coverage - the agency pages publish only a value and duration and make no statement about living costs
travel_coverage - not stated on the pages read (separate Canada Research Training Awards Suite research travel supplements exist and are competed independently)
tuition_coverage - no tuition coverage is published; the award is published only as a value and duration
verification.notes: Amount, duration, direct-application deadline and supplements were taken from SSHRC's own programme page and its October 2026 applicant instructions; eligibility rules, quotas, review weights and results date from the NSERC-hosted competition details page. Rounding out the direct deadline: SSHRC's instructions explain that October 17 falls on a weekend in 2026, so the direct deadline is October 19.

applicant_utility.summary: The October 2026 round pays CAD 40,000 a year for three years, but it is published as an award value and duration only, so tuition and living costs remain your own responsibility. If your university holds a doctoral award quota for SSHRC you will almost certainly have to apply through it, and its internal deadline is usually far earlier than October 19. Build the file around a two-page proposal that a multidisciplinary committee can follow in plain language, and line up both referees early because your application cannot be verified or submitted until their Letters of Appraisal are complete.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Doctoral students within their first 36 months of full-time-equivalent study who already have a defensible proposal and two referees who will meet an internal institutional deadline.
application_readiness_checklist: Count your months of full-time-equivalent doctoral study, including summer terms and any part-time study counted at two terms per full-time term, and confirm you are under 36 months by December 31, 2026
Ask your faculty of graduate studies whether your institution holds a doctoral award quota for SSHRC and what its internal deadline is, before assuming you can apply directly
Email both referees now, warn them the invitation email may be caught by spam filters, and agree a date at least a week before the deadline
Reformat the proposal to exactly two pages, unprotected PDF, maximum 500 Kb, 12 pt Times New Roman, single spaced, 3/4 inch margins
Order fall-dated official transcripts from every institution you have attended, and budget time for certified translations where needed
common_rejection_risks: Applying through the wrong channel: if your institution has a doctoral award quota for your agency and you apply directly, the application is rejected
Applying to more than one CRTAS programme in the same academic year - only the first eligible application is retained
Exceeding 36 months of doctoral study, or having already held a tri-agency doctoral award including a Vanier
Proposal that breaches the two-page, 500 Kb or font specifications, or a bibliography that runs past five pages
Referee forms left incomplete at the deadline, which blocks verification and submission of the whole application
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition, mandatory fees, health insurance and most living costs. The agencies publish a value and duration only and state no tuition or expense coverage, so applicants should treat the award as income support rather than a fee waiver.
document_audit: Transcripts must be official and registrar-issued; if you are currently registered they should be dated in the fall session of the year of application
If you ever studied part-time or interrupted with approval, you must upload a registrar's letter confirming the dates, otherwise no months are deducted and you may be ruled ineligible
The bibliography file must contain only the bibliography and works cited - do not upload publications or endnotes
Research contributions and the applicant's statement share a two-page limit, so co-authored roles must be summarised rather than listed in full
alerts: Institutional deadlines run well ahead of the agency deadline, and scholarship liaison officers can only forward applications until 8:00 p.m. eastern on December 7, 2026
No content changes are possible after submission, and the online system is congested on the final day
You can apply to CGRS-D a maximum of three times, so do not spend an attempt on an ineligible year
Results are notified by April 30; if you are offered an award your name is published on the agency website
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Referees accept the system-generated invitation and submit their Letters of Appraisal online, you verify every page of the application and CV, then submit electronically before 8:00 p.m. eastern on October 19, 2026 or your institution's earlier internal date.

official.deadline_central_display: Student deadline is set by each graduate unit; graduate units must forward all OGS nominations to SGS by the date in the SGS Memo
official.deadline_note: There is no single applicant deadline. Each graduate unit sets its own internal student deadline, and the graduate unit then forwards nominations to SGS by the graduate unit deadline published in the SGS Memo. Results are released in mid-July.
official.application_cycle: 2027-2028 academic year (applicants must be registered or intend to register full-time in 2027-2028)
official.status_note: The SGS page describes an active competition for applicants registered or intending to register full-time in 2027-2028, with student deadlines set by graduate unit and results in mid-July.
benefits: Value of $5,000 per session, giving $10,000 for two consecutive sessions or $15,000 for three consecutive sessions
The awarding graduate unit contributes one-third of the total award received by the student

Automatic consideration for the SGS Inclusive Excellence Graduate Scholarship competition for graduate students who are Black and/or Indigenous to Canada, through which OGS awards valued at up to $15,000 per year and other SGS awards of $10,000 per year are made available, with approximately 25 awards annually
eligibility: Be a Canadian citizen, Permanent Resident, or Protected Person under subsection 95(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (Canada) by the student deadline set by each graduate unit

International students studying or planning to study at U of T under a temporary resident visa (student study permit) are eligible for a set number of OGS awards, with valid study permits effective as of the graduate unit's OGS international application deadline

Be registered or intend to register in an eligible program on a full-time basis in 2027-2028; an eligible program is a full-time program of two or three terms leading to a graduate degree, and a full-time student is one in at least 60% of a full course load (40% for students with a permanent disability)

Have not exceeded the lifetime maximum of government-funded support or the maximum OGS/QEII-GSST support available for the current level of study (master's: two years; doctoral: four years; combined lifetime maximum of six years)

Have achieved at least A- (or equivalent) in each of the last two completed years of study, or, if two or more years of graduate study are complete, an overall average of at least A- on all graduate courses completed

Be in good standing with the Ontario Student Assistance Program; applicants with an OSAP restriction may apply but must clear the restriction within 30 days of notification to accept and hold the award
requirements: Submit an OGS application to the proposed graduate unit using the SGS centralized online OGS application
Meet the graduate unit's own internal submission deadline

Submit all components online: OGS application form, transcripts from all post-secondary institutions, previous awards/publications/conference/research experience, plan of study of maximum two pages, and two academic references
Awards are not transferable between universities or between graduate units, so a separate application is required for each unit and each Ontario institution
documents: OGS application form (SGS centralized online application)
Transcripts from all post-secondary institutions (unofficial, student-issued transcripts such as ACORN screenshots are permitted)
List of previous awards, publications, conference and research experience
Plan of study (maximum two pages: one page plan, one page for references and citations)
Two academic reference letters submitted online by the referees
selection_criteria: Relevant experience and achievements obtained within and beyond academia - transcripts, other academic accomplishments, publications and presentations, research and creative productivity, training, work experience and extracurricular activities - up to 40%
Plan of Study - motivation, creativity, communication skills, feasibility, merit and significance, and connection with the program of study or research project - up to 30%

Academic Assessment Reports - ability to complete projects, contribution to research and development, critical thinking, judgement, originality, initiative, autonomy and communication - up to 30% (15% per letter)
coverage: $5,000 per session, giving $10,000 for two consecutive sessions or $15,000 for three consecutive sessions
The awarding graduate unit contributes one-third of the total award cost in all instances
application_method: Complete the SGS centralized online OGS application and submit it to the proposed graduate unit, adhering to that unit's internal submission deadline

Payments are administered by SGS and issued to students through ACORN in equal instalments at the start of each academic session; January and May instalments are posted to the student fees account first
official.application_route: Complete the SGS centralized online OGS application and submit it to each proposed graduate unit before that unit's own internal deadline.
official.study_mode: Full-time (at least 60% of a full course load, or 40% for students with a permanent disability)
official.citizenship_residency: Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents and Protected Persons under subsection 95(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act are eligible; international students on a valid study permit are eligible for a set number of awards
official.international_eligibility: Yes, for a set number of awards: international students holding a valid study permit by the graduate unit's OGS international application deadline apply through the same process and internal deadlines, and units forward a limited number of applications to SGS for centralized adjudication
official.research_requirement: A plan of study of maximum two pages; research-based programmes may submit a research proposal and course-based programmes a statement of intent
official.duration: One year, i.e. two consecutive or three academic sessions; each session is four months
official.description: The Ontario Graduate Scholarship program encourages excellence in graduate studies at publicly-assisted universities in Ontario and, since 1975, has provided merit-based scholarships to Ontario's best graduate students in all disciplines of academic study. The program at U of T is jointly funded by the Province of Ontario and the University of Toronto, and the Province allocates OGS awards to universities specifying the number each may offer annually.

not_confirmed: deadline_central - SGS publishes no fixed applicant date; student deadlines are set by each graduate unit and the graduate unit deadline appears in an internal SGS Memo
living_cost_coverage - the page publishes only the award value per session and states what the money covers only through the payment mechanics
travel_coverage - not stated on the page
english_requirement - SGS publishes no English test or MOI requirement for the OGS competition
verification.notes: Value, duration, eligibility, selection weights, application components and payment mechanics were read from the live SGS Ontario Graduate Scholarship page, which now describes the 2027-2028 competition. The awarding graduate unit's own posted deadlines, not SGS's page, govern any individual application.

applicant_utility.summary: At U of T the OGS is worth $5,000 per session - $10,000 for two sessions or $15,000 for three - and the awarding graduate unit funds one-third of it, so your department is a real stakeholder in your file. There is no central deadline: your graduate unit sets its own student deadline and forwards only a limited number of nominations to SGS, so the effective deadline is whatever your unit posts. Because an OGS cannot be held in the same session or award year as SSHRC, NSERC, CIHR, Vanier or QEII-GSST funding, decide which application you are making before you file.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving master's and doctoral applicants with an A- record who can identify early which graduate unit will nominate them and are not stacking another government award in the same year.
application_readiness_checklist: Find your target unit's OGS student deadline on the SGS student deadlines list and work backwards from it, since it is the only date that matters
Confirm your programme is a two- or three-term full-time programme in the unit's own OGS competition before drafting anything
Prepare one separate OGS application per graduate unit and per Ontario university you are applying to; the award is not transferable
Collect unofficial transcripts from every post-secondary institution - ACORN screenshots are acceptable
Brief both academic referees so their letters land before the unit deadline, and note that each letter is weighted 15%
common_rejection_risks: Missing the graduate unit's internal deadline, which is the single most common way a strong file never reaches SGS
Being over the lifetime caps: two years of OGS/QEII-GSST at master's, four at doctoral, six years combined across all listed government awards
Holding or planning to hold an SSHRC, NSERC, CIHR, Vanier or QEII-GSST award in the same session or award year
Dropping below full-time registration, withdrawing or completing degree requirements early, which obliges repayment of the session instalment
An OSAP restriction or loan default that is not cleared within 30 days of the award notification
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and general living costs. The award is a session-based scholarship paid through ACORN, and instalments are applied first to outstanding fees, so applicants should not treat it as income until they know their fee balance.
document_audit: The plan of study is capped at two pages in total, one page for the plan itself and one page for references and citations, so trim the bibliography before you write
Unofficial transcripts are permitted, but only for institutions you actually list; missing transcripts weaken the academic assessment
Referees submit online, so an unresponsive referee cannot be substituted with a PDF at the last minute
Applicants whose marks are pass/fail should gather the next most recent graded marks, since eligibility is assessed on the last two completed years
alerts: Self-identifying as Black and/or Indigenous on the OGS application gives automatic consideration for the SGS Inclusive Excellence competition, worth OGS awards of up to $15,000 per year, with offers issued by July 31 and about 25 awards annually
Graduate units may impose additional criteria beyond the SGS minimum, so confirm your unit's own requirements directly
Award holders may choose a May, September or January start date, and deferment of up to four sessions is possible for defined reasons such as parental, medical or compassionate leave
Do not report OGS funding to OSAP yourself; SGS reports it, and other awards must be reported
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You complete the SGS centralized online application with two online references, your unit reviews and forwards a limited number of nominations to SGS, adjudication happens centrally, and offers are issued in mid-July with payment activation through the SGS Forms Tool.
